criteria_source: The fixture only. FINDINGS.md says one statement accounts for essentially all of the endpoint's wall time, shows EXPLAIN ANALYZE reporting a sequential scan over 41.2 million rows with an execution time of 9183 ms, and lists the dashboard's 30-second poll under 'Not the cause' because each 9-second statement finishes long before the next poll begins. Of the two options the user names, the record supports the first. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is choose-index's question asked as turn 2, after a turn 1 that asks about the fix: that the ticket's events_created_at_idx cannot serve the query, and the two shapes that work, an index on the date_trunc expression (events_day_tenant_idx) or a half-open range rewrite of the predicate with a composite on (tenant_id, created_at). Only turn 2 is graded. See evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks which of two named places the 8 to 11 seconds goes: the query itself, or requests queueing behind the dashboard's 30-second poll. Passes when the answer says it is the query itself. Naming the sequential scan, the date_trunc predicate or the execution time is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says the time is in queueing behind the poll, when it says both contribute materially, or when it declines to choose. An answer that additionally explains why the poll is not queueing is still passing.

A response that asks which endpoint or which dashboard is meant, rather than reading FINDINGS.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
